claims.text: The starting material is CoCrFeNi without solid-lubricant additions.
The intervention is addition of 2-5 wt% MoS2 to CoCrFeNi by powder metallurgy followed by consolidation and sintering.
Powder processing will produce MoS2 particles dispersed within the CoCrFeNi matrix.
Dispersed MoS2 will form a tribofilm during sliding.
At low temperatures, MoS2 reduces interfacial shear strength and acts as a solid lubricant.
At elevated temperatures, MoS2 may oxidize to MoO3.
MoO3 formed at elevated temperature may provide lubrication or surface protection.
MoS2 and its reaction products will inhibit direct metal-metal contact.
Inhibiting direct contact will reduce adhesive and abrasive wear.
The CoCrFeNi-MoS2 composite will have a coefficient of friction at least 20-40% below that of unmodified CoCrFeNi throughout 25-800 °C.
The CoCrFeNi-MoS2 composite will have a wear rate at least 30-50% below that of unmodified CoCrFeNi throughout 25-800 °C.
The proposed effectiveness applies in air at 25-800 °C, with 2-5 wt% MoS2 and loads no greater than 20 N.
Performance may differ at higher loads, in vacuum, or above 10 wt% MoS2.
The controlled experiment compares unmodified CoCrFeNi with CoCrFeNi containing 3 wt% MoS2 in air at 25, 400, and 800 °C under a 10 N load.
The hypothesis is declared falsified if the composite fails to achieve both at least 20% lower friction and at least 30% lower wear than the baseline at all tested temperatures.
